sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Columbus
sections.html:
Because Columbus and Muscogee County merged into one government, a single Tax Commissioner mails every bill and receives every payment in the city. Taxability and value are decided by the Muscogee County Board of Tax Assessors, whose members serve fixed terms under state law and are appointed by City Council.

Council fixes the mill rate for city operations. For the schools, the school board recommends a rate and Council, with few exceptions, must adopt it. Since 2016 Georgia has levied no state ad valorem tax. Grand jury appointees from Muscogee County make up the Board of Equalization, which the Clerk of Superior Court runs.

  • Tax Commissioner: billing, collection, delinquent accounts, tax sales.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: values, exemptions, appeals. Help desk: 706-225-4398.
  • Board of Equalization: disputes over value, uniformity and exemptions.

The assessors meet Wednesdays at 9:00am at the City Services Building, 3111 Citizens Way.

Columbus is the Muscogee County seat, on the Chattahoochee River opposite Phenix City, Alabama, roughly 100 miles southwest of Atlanta. Only one Georgia city is bigger.

Population was estimated at 202,171 in 2025, a 2.3% drop since 2020. Just 50.8% of homes are owner-occupied. The typical owned home is valued at $193,900, and rent averages $1,106. With so many rentals, plenty of Columbus sellers are landlords, and a rental's tax bill follows the January 1 owner like any other.

The Tax Commissioner lays out the year month by month: notices of assessment in May, bills in August, first payment in October.

Columbus property tax dates by month
MonthWhat happens
April 1Mobile home bills due; homestead deadline; business personal property, aircraft and watercraft returns due
MayAnnual notice of assessment mailed; appeals within 45 days of the notice date
JulyTaxing authorities advertise and set millage rates
AugustReal and personal property bills mailed
OctoberBills due: a 40% installment or payment in full
DecemberRemaining 60% due

During the appeal window you can file a homestead application instead of an appeal. Exact payment days are on your bill.

Owners may pay 40% in October and the other 60% in December, or settle everything in October. If your sale closes between the two payments, tell the title company what has already been paid.

Legal responsibility for a year's tax rests with the January 1 owner, whoever holds the house afterward. Buyer and seller can both receive a bill. The office leaves the question of who pays what share to the closing documents.

Should the tax go unpaid, the lien attaches to the January 1 owner, unless the seller shows within 90 days of the due date that the buyer assumed the liability. Acceptable proof is a recorded deed naming the new owner or closing language plainly assigning the tax to the buyer. After verification the lien may be recorded against the buyer instead.

The standard exemption cuts assessed value by $13,500. The Tax Commissioner also lists exemptions for age, military service and surviving spouses. File any time after the property becomes your primary residence, with April 1 as the last day for the year you want it.

  • Standard homestead (H1): $13,500 off assessed value for county and school board maintenance and operation levies, but not bond debt.
  • Elderly general (H2): 65 or older by January 1, household net income no higher than $10,000 the year before, with income documents.
  • Disabled veteran (H5): up to $121,812, with a VA benefits letter.
  • Unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in war or armed conflict: up to $121,812, backed by Department of Defense papers.
  • Surviving spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed or fatally hurt on duty: full 100% exemption.

Bring the recorded deed and a Georgia driver's license with your current address. Voter and vehicle registration must both be in Muscogee County. After approval the exemption renews until you move, the ownership changes or you seek a different one. A property tax deferral exists for owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less, running until a change of ownership or until the deferred tax and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

Start with what you owe today. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff figure, then share it with the title company so the closing statement shows the right amount. If the sale will close between the October and December payments, note which installment is paid.

  • Find your most recent notice of assessment and keep it with the deed.
  • Note whether a homestead exemption is on the house, since the buyer must apply for their own.
  • If the buyer will take over the year's tax, make sure the closing documents say so in plain words and get a recorded deed in the buyer's name, so the 90-day proof is ready.
  • For a rental, tell the tenants about the sale and keep the lease with the closing file.

A cash buyer can often move faster than a lender-backed one, but the same tax steps apply either way.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid property tax?
sections.html:
The Muscogee County Tax Commissioner can place a tax lien, called a fifa, and levy the property for a tax sale. The office does not sell its tax liens or lien certificates, and a property that fails to sell at a tax sale goes back into rotation for later sales. The Delinquent Tax section includes a tax sale list and a class registration page for bidders.

Staff cannot give legal advice, and owners with a lien or levy are told to consult an attorney. For a seller, the practical sequence is simple: get the payoff from the Tax Commissioner, confirm it with the title company, and clear the lien from the sale proceeds if the house sells before a tax sale date. A cash sale suits this well, because the payoff and title work are the only steps between you and the closing table.

Personal property has its own rule. Taxable tangible personal property other than motor vehicles, trailers and mobile homes is exempt when its total fair market value, as determined by the assessors, does not exceed $20,000.

Appeals are due 45 days after the date on the notice of assessment, which goes out in May. The Board of Tax Assessors receives and reviews the appeal, and the Board of Equalization hears matters of value, uniformity, taxability and denied exemptions.

Real property appeals go to ccgboa@columbusga.org, and personal property appeals go to ppboa@columbusga.org. Questions about real property appeals can also go to 706-225-4398. A homeowner who has not yet claimed a homestead can file that application during the same appeal period instead of appealing.

Keep the notice itself. It states the value the county will use for the bill, and the 45 days run from the date printed on it.

faqs.q: When are Columbus property tax bills due?
faqs.a: In October, as either a 40% installment or payment in full, with the remaining 60% due in December. The exact day is printed on your bill.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for Columbus property tax after I sell?
faqs.a: The person who owned the property on January 1 is legally responsible for that year's tax. Closing documents normally divide it, and a lien moves to the buyer only with proof delivered within 90 days of the due date.

faqs.q: How much is the standard homestead exemption in Columbus?
faqs.a: It is a $13,500 reduction in assessed value. It applies to the county and school maintenance and operation levies, not the bond portion.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline in Columbus?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, which is mailed in May. A homestead application can be filed in place of an appeal during that window.

faqs.q: Does the Columbus Tax Commissioner sell tax liens?
faqs.a: No. The office does not sell its tax liens or lien certificates. A property that does not sell at a tax sale returns to the rotation for future sales.
